A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PreferDiff. All 32 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original recommendation experiments, zero-shot transfer results, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, initialization and history-length studies, runtime measurements, and DPO comparisons in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The ranking objective, variational surrogate, cosine error, negative-centroid approximation, generation/preference mixture, and DDIM inference remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix. The initialization revision concerns experimental settings rather than a redesigned method.

E1.justification: V2 adds MovieLens-1M and Yahoo!R1 populations and evaluates fully trained recommendation on Steam, previously used for transfer evaluation. The existing Amazon leave-one-out and general recommendation datasets remain; they are not new additions.

E2.justification: Table 20 newly evaluates DreamRec combined with DPO and Diffusion-DPO, directly testing two important alternative preference objectives. Appendix F.4 also expands efficiency comparisons beyond DreamRec to SASRec, BERT4Rec, and TIGER. The later tables' TIGIR spelling refers to the existing TIGER comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 changes the reported initialization from Xavier to standard normal; unchanged original scores do not establish that experiments were rerun. New experiments introduce a 50,000-user Yahoo sample, history lengths of 10–50, initialization controls, denoising-step sweeps, and DPO beta values of 1, 5, and 10.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds history-length sensitivity, initialization comparisons, embedding-covariance analysis, broader efficiency measurements, and accuracy–latency trade-offs. It also reports unsuccessful dimensionality-reduction and covariance-regularization attempts. The original component, embedding-size, negative-count, guidance, and lambda analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report t-test significance at the 0.05 threshold. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original performance tables retain their scores, while Tables 14–20 add substantial results. Examples include ML-1M Recall@5 of 0.0629 and Sports Recall@5 of 0.0162 with one denoising step versus 0.0185 with twenty steps. These are newly reported evaluations, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The original objective derivations, DPO special-case relationship, and Appendix B–C mathematics remain unchanged. Appendix F.3 adds a variance-propagation derivation linking embedding covariance to variance-preserving diffusion, explicitly presenting the dimensionality explanation as a hypothesis without a rigorous proof.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim of a proved conditional equivalence to DPO with a more cautious connection from a preference-learning perspective. The abstract expands its stated benchmark validation from three to six. The central method, novelty, ranking, and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation of dimensionality and initialization sensitivity through a variance-preservation hypothesis. It adds failed-remedy observations, possible variance-exploding alternatives, and practical latency limitations. Appendix D.3 also explains baseline discrepancies through evaluation protocols. The original conclusion's dimension and lambda limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 revises the initialization instruction and documents preprocessing and sampling for the added datasets, DPO beta settings, and detailed training/inference costs. Existing hardware, optimizer, baseline implementations, and principal hyperparameter-search tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references, including work on softmax DPO and language-model recommendation. Appendix F.6 sharpens the distinction from DPO and Diffusion-DPO through cosine loss, multiple negatives, and reference-free training. The broader related-work organization and positioning in Appendix A remain stable.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, selected passages receive language corrections and clarifications, and Section 4.3 is modestly reordered. Appendix F and acknowledgments are added. Most existing methodological exposition and appendix prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 14–20 and Figures 9–12, displaying new benchmark comparisons, initialization results, covariance maps, and efficiency trade-offs; some plots redisplay tabulated measurements. Table 5 gains dataset columns. Algorithm 1 and the existing lambda figure move to the appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation by testing additional populations, direct DPO alternatives, and previously untested initialization and latency sensitivities. The standard-normal initialization instruction is particularly useful for reproduction given Table 17's severe degradation with Xavier initialization. These gains address important evidential gaps in v1, although uncertainty reporting remains limited, timing units are inconsistent between Table 18 and F.5, and the new variance explanation remains a hypothesis.
